brief: Issues signed SAML assertions for registered services, so a service provider can be developed and tested without an external identity provider.
detail: Assertions are signed by the engine with ECDSA-SHA256 over a P-256 key (random, or derived from a seed for repeatable tests) or with RSA-SHA256 over a key you supply or generate. Only a registered service can be the audience: an identity provider that vouches for any service that asks is an open redirect for identity. Subject and audience are escaped for & < and > before they enter the XML, so a subject holding markup cannot inject elements (checked with a quote, angle brackets and an ampersand); the issuer entity id, set by the operator, is written as given. The private key never leaves the object: PublicKey and TrustMeOn hand over only what a service provider needs. Use invented identities and keys in tests.
